Writing

Notes on where I think AI tooling is going, written between 2025 and 2026. Most of what I am building now started as one of these.

Developers: Don't Build a Machine. Build a Living Organism 2026-07-16

The mechanical worldview built the last seventy years of software. It's the wrong mental model for the next seventy.
Welcome to the Unstructured, Self-Documented API 2026-07-02

API contracts are rigid because the consumer used to be dumb. When the caller can read, negotiate, and adapt, the interface itself can finally loosen up.
We're Missing a Feedback Loop Platform for Normal Users 2026-06-25

AI researchers get RLHF pipelines and eval suites. The people who actually use AI all day get a thumbs-up icon. This asymmetry is a product gap, not a technical one.
Bye, User Signup. Hello Self-Registration 2026-06-08

The signup form assumes your user has an email inbox, a phone, and fingers. Your next million users will have none of these.
Infra Is Not Ready for the AI Era 2026-05-14

Every layer of cloud infrastructure assumes a human with a browser, a credit card, and infinite patience for dashboards. Agents have none of these. Why I'm building Interagentic.
Building Software That Morphs Itself 2026-04-20

Every user gets the same pixels because changing software used to require an engineer. It doesn't anymore. Notes from shipping UI that rewrites itself per user.
Security in the AI Era: Antivirus vs. Boundaries 2026-04-02

One school inspects behavior and hunts for bad patterns. The other makes bad outcomes structurally impossible. We already ran this experiment once — and pattern-matching lost.
Building Context as a Background Live Loop 2026-03-05

Agents assemble their understanding of you from scratch, per request, under time pressure. Real assistants never work this way — context should be built continuously, in the background.
Permissions Are the Main Brake on Useful AI. Treat Them as a Live System 2026-02-10

The capability ceiling of today's agents isn't intelligence — it's authorization. Static grants can't govern dynamic workers.
Meet the Living Software Stack 2026-01-15

Software has always been dead matter arranged by hand: written once, deployed, decayed. What happens when every layer of the stack can rewrite itself?
Tool Vibe-Coding as a Learning Mechanism 2025-12-02

Vibe-coding apps for humans churned. Vibe-coding tools for agents is a different animal entirely: the output has a spec, a test, and a user that never gets bored.
Don't Use AI to Build Software. Use It to Build Software Factories 2025-10-09

AI at build time beats AI at run time. The most leveraged thing an LLM can produce isn't an app — it's the machine that produces apps.
Software as a Means for AI to Program Its Own Brain 2025-09-11

Weights are read-only at runtime. Code isn't. The most practical form of self-improvement is an agent writing the software it will think with tomorrow.
From Copying, to Reasoning, to Trying: AI Needs to Learn at Runtime 2025-08-21

The third era of machine learning won't happen in a training run. And the surprising part: it doesn't need AI to work.
Software-Based Beats Token-Based 2025-07-24

Our approach to AI intelligence is wrong. AI will be dramatically better when we give it the tools we built for ourselves, instead of making it emulate them token by token.
Intelligence Is Here. Now We Need Better Tools 2025-06-12

The bottleneck has moved. Models are smart enough for most real work — what's missing is everything around them.
The Tech Stack Is Too Complex for AI — Because It Was Already Too Complex for Us 2025-05-08

AI didn't break software engineering. It exposed how broken it already was. Tech teams were inefficient long before the first token was sampled.
A DSL for GenUI Is So Much Better Than Pure React 2025-04-14

Letting a model emit raw React is handing a firehose to a calligrapher. Constrain the language and generation gets faster, safer, and dramatically more correct.
